source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 3 (ISL A3) · lesson 10. Rewritten for children from Dr. Hassan's lesson; facts and references kept.
topic: From dawn to sunset, for Allah

learn.en: Ṣawm means holding back. In Ramadan, Muslims hold back from food and drink from dawn (Fajr) until sunset, for Allah.
learn.title: What is fasting?

learn.en: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar. Fasting it is the fourth pillar of Islam. (Qur'an 2:183)
learn.title: The fourth pillar

learn.en: Grown-up Muslims who are healthy and not travelling must fast. If someone is ill or travelling, he can eat and make up the days later. (Qur'an 2:184)
learn.title: Who fasts?

learn.en: Suḥūr is the meal before dawn: “Take suḥūr, for there is blessing in it.” (Bukhari 1923) Ifṭār is breaking the fast at sunset — the Sunnah is with dates or water.
learn.title: Suḥūr and ifṭār

learn.en: Fasting is more than an empty tummy. If someone keeps lying, Allah has no need of him leaving his food and drink. (Bukhari 1903)
learn.title: Fast with your tongue too

quiz.en: From when until when do we fast?
Who may break the fast and make it up later?
True or false? There is blessing in suḥūr.
True or false? Lying doesn't matter when you're fasting.

think.q: If you try a half-day fast this Ramadan, what will you have for suḥūr and ifṭār?
think.a: Something healthy for suḥūr, and break your fast with a date and water, like the Prophet ﷺ.

parents.summary: Fasting Ramadan (the 9th month) is the 4th pillar: no food or drink from dawn to sunset. The ill and travellers make it up later. Suḥūr has blessing; ifṭār is on time, with dates.
parents.tip: Let your child try a few hours of fasting and break it with a date at the agreed time.
